notes: Katy Pye sent a typed letter to Susan Garwood which has additional information about the club: "I had an interesting conversation with my  Uncle, Edgar Pye, .... about the Nature Study Club's room in the Library. He said a small portion of the second floor reading room (separated by an 8 step walk-up) was dedicated to the Club. It contained nature books, a display of arrow heads, and framed mountings of North and South American butterflies. My great Uncle, Donald Loyhed, was working for a mining Company in South America and sent two sets of  Butterflies to his mother, Mrs. Edgar Lyhed. She had them framed and gave them to the Nature Study Club room where they hung for many years. Mrs. Grant gave the set of North American species and Mrs. Sheffield provided lovely furniture. Uncle Ed was musing over what may have happened to the Butterflies. He also remember the walls of the main second floor reading room were painted with lovely murals by a man from Carlton college.

Wikipedia:
The Grand Army of the Republic (GAR) was a fraternal organization composed of veterans of the Union Army who served in the American Civil War. Founded in 1866, it was dissolved in 1956 when its last member died. Linking men through their experience of the war, the GAR became among the first organized advocacy groups in American politics, supporting voting rights for black veterans, lobbying the US Congress to establish veterans' pensions, and supporting Republican political candidates. Its peak of membership at more than 400,000 was in 1890, a high point of Civil War commemorative ceremonies. It was succeeded by the Sons of Union Veterans of the Civil War (SUVCW), composed of male descendants of Union veterans.

descrip:
Items came from the Norma Wilkowske, Bohn, Sawle estate.  Norma was married three times (3 names).  Donor is her daughter.
The donation is very large and includes items that came to RCHS at different dates as Kathleen went through the estate.  Included are apparently items from the Wilkowske Hardware of Morristown as well as personal items from the family.  Norma was the Justice of Peace of Morristown so there are items from there as well.
dgname: Kathleen N. Wilkowske- trustee Norma Bohn-Sawle Trust
notes:
This donation came to RCHS in many boxes over a period of time, mainly in 2001.  It was stored  for years until someone was available to process it.  All items went before the Collections Com. where a decision was made as to what to do with each item.  Most of them were added to the collection, some were passed on to other organizations, most especially to the Morristown Historical Society.  Some items were discarded due to the condition of the item.  The items were sorted into several sections including: Farm related,  Business (Hardware store & other records seeminly related to the business) ,  Justice of the Peace papers, & Woodmen of the World.  Also, there were many objects & paper items such as programs etc. that have been grouped with related objects  in the collection. 
Care has been taken with the process, however due to the size of the collection and the time it has taken to process it some errors in numbering and filing may have occured.  If such is found please make corrections as needed and accept my appologies. Pat Chappuie

descrip: WWII uniform including hats and boots, army bag, and foot locker used by Melving Heyer.  Flecks Beer case and 2 Flecks bottles, 2 Voegel milk bottles.
instruct: Items can be used for educational purposes.
notes:
Information accompaning the donation:
The uniform was donated by the family of Melvin Heyer who was a lifelong resident of Rice County.  He served in World War II and was inducted into the U.S. Army on Aug. 16, 1941 and was honorably discharged on Oct. 5, 1946.  His rank at discharge was Tech 4 (the arm patches with the "T") which was equivalent to the rank of sergeant at that time. 
Melvin saw battle in Sicily, Rome-Arno, southern France, Rhineland, and Central Europe.  Melvin talked about seeing combat on D-Day as well.  He received a good conduct medal for GO#27339th Ordinance-43.  He also received the following medals: European- African Middle Eastern theater Service Medal, American Defense Service Medal, Five (5) Overseas Service Bars.
A picture of these medals that were on his uniform is also provided as the family wished to save them as a memory of him. 
In researching the pin with the 2 crossing rifles on the right shoulder of his uniform it would indicate that he was infantry.  The patches on his uniform provide an interesting history also.  On the right of the chest, there is a patch that looks like an eagle.  This represents an honorable service discharge for soldiers that had done their duty and for members of the army that had served between Dec. 7, 1941 and Dec. 31, 1946.  In researching the patch on the right shoulder that looks like the letter 'A' with seven steps, it denotes the seventh army.  The letter 'A' stood for "Army' and was surrounded by seven steprs, which indicated seven battles.  The blue signified infantry, the yellow signified calvary, and the red color signified artillery.  the patch on the left arm that looks like a sword in the middle of fire indicated the 63rd infantry division.  In researching this information, we found that apparently other soldiers were deployed with the 7th Army if they were trained and ready to go into battle. 
*this information is attached to the donation sheet.

notes:
Thrift Shop was started by donor's grandmother as "Shevlin's"  Donor's mother ran it as "Jan's Thrift Shop" 
*The shop originally was started two doors down from the last location by Lorraine & Warren Shevlin in 1967 (Jan's parents) as a garage sale in their basement.  They then created the thrift store because of its popularity.  Jan Hansen purchased the thrift shop in1989. Everyone grew up going there, starting their families. In 1992 Jan moved the thrift shop to its current location 200 ft. up the block.. Jan always put out the donated sign on the highway to let people know where the thrift shop was located because it used to be in the country, but later it was included in the city units. The thrift shop closed Dec. 2023 afer an estate sale.  Memory : there is a map on the wall (still in the building) where visitors could put a pin showing where they came from.
